transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-08-10
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Opal Head of Platform), Sofia Ruiz (Opal Solutions Architect), Ken Nakamura (Opal CTO)
Links shared: partner spec draft (https://redwood.app/partner-specs/opalsystems), security pack (drive link), sample benchmark CSV (redwood-bench-2026-07.csv)

Summary:
Quick partner intro + technical discovery to scope an onramp pilot for Opal's integrator offering (they want Redwood as a bundled inference runtime option through their marketplace). Focus: GPU compatibility, networking (VPC peering vs service-connect), operator model (managed vs air-gapped), telemetry & billing handoff.

Topics:
- Opal's fleet and SKU variability (A100 -> 80GB, H100 variants, Ampere v2)
- Private vs hosted routing (marketplace flow needs optional VPC/private deployment)
- KV cache & prefix caching semantics across multi-tenant instances
- Marketplace billing and revenue share, margin modeling
- Security: SSO/SAML, SOC2, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: all right hi everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, and with me is Liam our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Jordan: good, thanks. appreciate you taking the time. we've been trying to understand how we'd slot Redwood into our market place offering.
[00:12] Sofia: yeah hi, I'm Sofia, i own the integration side. we have a pretty heterogeneous GPU fleet and a couple of private on prem customers so, need to see workflow.
[00:20] Liam: great, quick intro from my side — I focus on infra compatibility and latency optimization. can you walk through the shapes and typical models you expect to surface?
[00:29] Ken: sure. we run A100 40 and 80, H100 in some pods, and a few Ampere V2 nodes for lower-cost lanes. most customers pick either hosted connectors or an on-prem plug.
[00:40] Jordan: our ask is: can Redwood be embedded as an option in our marketplace so that when a customer purchases an Opal package, they can opt into Redwood inference (hosted or private) and we handle the provisioning.
[00:51] Maya: totally, that's very aligned with other partners. a couple of immediate things we'll need to validate: model binary compatibility with your drivers (cuda versions etc), network egress patterns for hosted vs VPC, and if you want billing handoff — how you'd prefer tokens/usage reporting.
[01:03] Sofia: about the cuda/driver mismatch — some of our older clusters are on 11.4 and we've got mixed kubernetes distros. we do use a thin operator today to deploy inference containers.
[01:13] Liam: sounds familiar — we usually produce a compatibility matrix. we also have a tiny shim that sits as an operator sidecar to handle KV cache hot storage — sometimes transcription here shows 'k v cache' — but it's basically the local prefix / KV cache coordination.
[01:29] Jordan: okay the KV cache thing is interesting — if multiple tenants hit the same node we need to be sure it won't leak keys. is that multi-tenant safe by default?
[01:37] Liam: yes, we namespace caches by tenant id. though worth noting some customers choose to give us per-tenant Dedicated pools to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
[01:45] Ken: can we talk latency — customers in europe expect < 120ms for chat features. if Redwood is hosted in the US, we'd need either local edge or private deployment.
[01:56] Maya: we can route by region — we have hosted nodes in eu-west; for stricter SLOs we'd recommend Dedicated or Private VPC. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and you can reserve capacity to meet those p99s.
[02:07] Sofia: and for marketplace flow, ideally provisioning should be API-driven. can your control plane accept a programmatic provisioning call from Opal's provisioning pipeline?
[02:16] Liam: yes — we have a partner API for provisioning model endpoints and toggling private vs hosted modes. typical flow: Opal calls provision endpoint, we create a model deployment, return endpoint + secrets; for VPC/on-prem we return install manifests and a bootstrap token.
[02:30] Jordan: who owns the keys in the VPC flow? we need to be clear on KMS responsibilities.
[02:35] Maya: in Private mode Opal owns KMS; we can integrate with your KMS or HSM. in Dedicated the customer can bring their own key material too. we'll include a KMS integration doc in the follow-up.
[02:46] Ken: audit and logs — do you ship detailed request logs? some of our regulated customers need per-request metadata with redaction controls.
[02:54] Liam: yes we emit structured traces and token-level cost metadata, and we can redact or not store prompts. those are configurable retention policies. there may be storage implications for the telemetry.
[03:05] Sofia: on pricing — we need an easy rev-share model we can surface in the marketplace. are you comfortable with revenue share or do you prefer reseller/resale?
[03:14] Maya: we do both. for partner marketplaces we commonly do a split (you bill the customer, send us usage reports + invoice Opal pays Redwood net of your cut) or we can do pass-through where Redwood bills and shares a marketplace commission. we'll send sample contracts.
[03:27] Jordan: ok that helps. also — can Redwood publish a small benchmark for our H100 pods? we want to show customers expected latency/cost combos.
[03:35] Liam: absolutely, we can run a brief micro-benchmark — can you provide a small model artifact or we'll run with a standard LLM we support. it would need ~4 hours on those nodes to get representative numbers.
[03:45] Ken: timeline — we're aiming for a soft beta in 6 weeks if security signoff is fast.
[03:50] Maya: 6 weeks is tight but doable for a focused pilot. immediate blockers to unblock: SOC2 attestation, MSA redlines, shared infra manifests, and sample workloads.
[04:01] Sofia: on SOC2 we require the report plus an architecture diagram. also SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and want user mapping into our RBAC system.
[04:11] Liam: we support SAML and OIDC; for partner integrations we map SAML attributes into tenant roles. we'll include a SSO notes doc.
[04:19] Jordan: a couple of deeper technical questions from our infra team — how do you do model fallbacks? we expect to route to a cheaper model if capacity is constrained.
[04:28] Liam: we support automated routing policies — you can define latency or cost thresholds and fallback to a compatible model variant, or route to a lower-cost quantized replica. the important piece is tokenizer/response parity so we recommend the same family of models for fallbacks.
[04:41] Ken: can that routing be done at the marketplace layer (Opal) or must it be configured in Redwood?
[04:46] Maya: either — we expose routing policies via API so Opal can orchestrate; or Redwood can automatically enforce fallbacks based on capacity. most partners prefer Opal control for marketplace UX.
[04:57] Sofia: any constraints around multi-tenant caching? e.g. prefix cache warmups between different customers?
[05:03] Liam: we namespace keys and have cache invalidation hooks. there is a warmup cost if you switch models or tenants frequently. for predictable latency, recommended to pre-warm common prefixes or use Dedicated for high QPS customers.
[05:15] Jordan: about the operator — you mentioned a small sidecar — what privileges does it need? we have strict PodSecurityPolicies.
[05:22] Liam: minimal privileges: read mounts for KV cache path, network to control-plane endpoints, and ability to create a local cache directory. we can run it as non-root and support PSP-compliant manifests.
[05:32] Ken: we also need to understand failover — if the opal node loses connectivity to Redwood control plane, what's the behavior?
[05:38] Liam: the agent keeps running local deployments; for hosted/managed we have a degradation mode where requests either queue or failover to a smaller local model if configured. we'll document the exact state transitions.
[05:50] Maya: okay we're getting deep which is great. quick callouts: we'll produce a compatibility matrix, a demo plan for the micro-benchmark, an integration playbook for your marketplace flow, and a draft commercial term example.
[06:02] Sofia: sounds good. about the demo — would you run a playback with our infra team where you do an install and show the routing?
[06:10] Liam: yes, plan a technical demo + live install. recommend separate SE session with your infra.
[06:16] Jordan: timeline again — if we aim for beta week of Aug 24th what are the concrete milestones?
[06:22] Maya: milestone 1 (this week): share infra manifests & SOC2; milestone 2 (by Aug 17): Redwood compatibility report + pricing sample; milestone 3 (Aug 24): pilot kickoff with infra + SE; milestone 4 (end of pilot): evaluate metrics and next steps.
[06:38] Ken: one more ask — we sometimes resell partner services under our contracts, need MSA language for reseller and liability limits.
[06:45] Maya: we'll include reseller clause examples and typical liability caps; legal can follow up.
[06:51] Jordan: competitors — some customers ask about PaloCloud and GigaServe; we want clear differentiation (cost, observable telemetry, and on-prem controls).
[06:59] Liam: differentiation: token-level cost telemetry, automatic prefix/KV caching, and unified API between hosted/dedicated/private. we'll include a one-pager.
[07:09] Sofia: ok let's capture action items.
[07:12] Maya: i'll summarize and send notes — any other questions?
[07:16] Ken: none from me. thanks.
[07:18] Jordan: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
